headline: CISA deadlines for exploited N-able and MONAI Label flaws fall on 26 November
plain_summary: CISA has set 26 November as the fix date for exploited flaws in N-able Mail Assure and the MONAI Label medical imaging tool, and 1 and 2 December for Puppet Enterprise and LiteLLM. A hospital in Guadeloupe says all its data was encrypted, and a medical supplier reports a breach affecting 1,326,066 people. An F5 BIG-IP flaw has public exploit code. Organisations running the named products should apply the vendor fixes.

items.title: N-able Mail Assure server accessed; related flaw due 26 November
items.why: N-able confirms attackers accessed one hosted server and a separate flaw, CVE-2026-134624, was found during the investigation.
items.action: As The Hacker News reports N-able advisory, SpamExperts Local Cloud operators should confirm they run build 20261121.1943; Hosted Cloud users have nothing to install.

items.title: Amazon: AI agents exploited a MONAI Label zero-day
items.why: Amazon says the flaw, CVE-2026-133968, gave root on a server; the developing report differs on whether a fix is out.
items.action: ENISA lists MONAI Label versions before 0.8.6 as affected; follow the maintainers advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94.

items.title: CISA adds exploited Puppet Enterprise flaw; fix due 1 December
items.why: A client with a Puppet CA-signed certificate can run code as the Puppet Server user.
items.action: Upgrade Puppet Enterprise to 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 or 2023.8.13 and restart the server, per Help Net Security.

items.title: CISA adds Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap flaws
items.why: CISA cites active exploitation; the LiteLLM deadline is 2 December.
items.action: Find Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap in your environment and apply vendor fixes where they exist; Axis 1.x is reported end of life.

items.title: F5 BIG-IP flaw CVE-2026-126714 has public exploit code
items.why: HKCERT says an authenticated attacker could run system commands on affected versions.
items.action: Apply the workarounds in F5 advisory K000164320 for BIG-IP 17.1.0 - 17.1.3, 17.5.0 - 17.5.1 and 21.1.0.

items.title: CHU de Guadeloupe says all its data was encrypted
items.why: The hospital has postponed non-urgent care; no ransom demand had been received as of 23 November.
items.action: Call the emergency medical line before going to the hospital, as SAMU doctor Patrick Portecop advises; urgent care continues.

items.title: Prism Medical Products breach affects 1,326,066 people
items.why: The company confirms suspicious activity on 19 October; data includes names and, for some, Social Security and medical details.
items.action: Prism is mailing notification letters and offering 24 months of credit monitoring and dark web monitoring, per HIPAA Journal.
